chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from 'Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam from his father who said:

I walked with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in al-Baqi', and we passed by the grave of a man from the people of Kufa from the Shia. I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, this is the grave of a man from the Shia.'

So he (peace be upon him) stood by it and then said: 'O God, have mercy on his strangeness (being away from home), connect his solitude, comfort his loneliness, and send down to him from Your mercy a mercy with which he will be content with instead of the mercy of anyone other than You, and join him with whomever was his guardian.'
Then he recited: 'Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree,' seven times.

key_terms.الغُرْبَة: Strangeness or being away from one's homeland, often referring to the state of the deceased in the grave
key_terms.الْبَقِيعُ: Al-Baqi', a famous cemetery in Medina

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for a deceased Shia according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia practice of visiting graves (Ziyarat) and the Imam’s intercessory role, specifically invoking God to alleviate the spiritual loneliness (*ghurba*) of the deceased. The unique ritual of reciting Surah al-Qadr seven times underscores the belief in the night of decree as a time of divine mercy and elevation, linking the deceased’s status to the blessings of the Quran’s revelation. It reflects the scholarly emphasis on the spiritual companionship of the Imams with the faithful even after death.
